points.title: SOP-504: Statutory Integrity Standards for Refinery Pressure Vessels
points.text: --- PAGE 1 --- CONFIDENTIAL INTERNAL STANDARD — HEALTH, SAFETY & ENVIRONMENT (HSE) SOP-504: STATUTORY INTEGRITY STANDARDS FOR REFINERY PRESSURE VESSELS Standard Code: NRC-HSE-SOP-504-REV-04 | Classification: STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL SECTION 1.0 — OBJECTIVE & JURISDICTION This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes mandatory safety envelopes, minimum retirement wall thicknesses, and shutdown criteria for all high-temperature pressure vessels, columns, and heat exchangers across refinery operational units. SECTION 3.2 — MINIMUM RETIREMENT WALL THICKNESS CRITERIA Under no operational circumstances shall any pressure boundary component operate below the calculated minimum retirement thickness (t_min) determined in accordance with ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII. Any measurement indicating wall thickness below t_min constitutes an IMMEDIATE CRITICAL NON-CONFORMANCE requiring immediate de-pressurization and formal approval by the Refinery Safety Director before re-pressurization. SECTION 4.1 — PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PRV) MANDATORY TOLERANCE All PRVs protecting hydrocarbon distillation columns must be bench-calibrated every 12 months. Allowable set-pressure deviation is strictly limited to +/- 1.5%. Any premature seat leakage below 90% of set-pressure or reseat delay exceeding 3.0 seconds requires immediate valve replacement with a certified backup unit prior to start-up. SECTION 5.4 — CLADDING INTEGRITY & NAPHTHENIC CORROSION Where crude feeds contain Total Acid Number (TAN) exceeding 0.5 mg KOH/g, stainless steel cladding delamination exceeding 100 cm² requires shutdown weld repair. Operating unclad carbon steel at temperatures above 230°C in high-TAN service is strictly prohibited. Approved By: Dr. A. Sharma, Director of Plant Safety & Oversight | Approved: 2025-06-01
